statusNote: All Acceptance Criteria of the canonical GitHub Issue #23 are met. The reviewer's authoritative Required Command sweep passed in the exact frozen forms, and make verify was re-run against the committed tree at 9c53be7d5a49aaf69e371c83f2ac3e6ce3df17d3 with all 19 named gates passing at exit 0; see reviewerFinalResults.makeVerifyCommittedHead. Two supplemental observations remain outstanding and are recorded honestly as Tier-H limitations rather than as failed criteria: the real Accessibility prompt was never visibly seen, and no same-process grant-to-revoke transition was demonstrated. The Issue requires neither, so neither blocks acceptance. See manual.md and manualProbeCommands.reviewerRuns.

manualProbeCommands.purpose: Tier-H manual harness only. Not an automated acceptance command, not part of the Required Command sweep, and not a substitute for any gate. It exists because M1-035 adds no app wiring, so the manual steps otherwise had no executable entry point.
manualProbeCommands.defaultState: Skipped when the variable is unset or empty, so no ordinary run can ask macOS to display OS UI.
manualProbeCommands.requestSemantics: The request action submits kAXTrustedCheckOptionPrompt as true, which requests macOS to display a prompt and returns immediately. macOS decides whether to display it and can suppress redisplay for an existing TCC decision. If macOS displays it, the reviewer can observe it. No prompt was observed for M1-035 and none is claimed.

reviewerRuns.source: Reported by the coordinating Codex reviewer on the 2026-09-22 UTC observation day, against commit 9c53be7d5a49aaf69e371c83f2ac3e6ce3df17d3. Transcribed by the author, who observed none of it.
reviewerRuns.machineReadableRecord: manual-result.json records these same runs in closed-vocabulary form, and manual-output.log carries their sanitized output lines verbatim.

runs.demonstrates: The real AXIsProcessTrusted path returns trusted for a responsible identity that genuinely holds Accessibility authorization, through the production default with no seam substituted. Together with the notTrusted runs under the Claude Code and Claude Opus 5 identities, both real trust states were observed on real macOS. This satisfies the Issue Scope item 'check'.

runs.reviewerObservation: The reviewer visually confirmed that System Settings opened and showed the Accessibility permissions list.
runs.notClaimed: This is not evidence of a deep link. The implementation opens the System Settings application only; the Accessibility pane was already the selected pane. Known limitation 1 is unchanged.

runs.reviewerObservation: No OS prompt was visibly observed. The request itself ran to completion and exited 0.
runs.inference: A pre-existing denied TCC decision for the responsible identity plausibly suppressed redisplay of the prompt. This is recorded as an inference, not as an observation, and it is not offered as evidence that the prompt is displayed.
runs.notDemonstrated: That macOS displayed its Accessibility prompt. The call requests macOS to display one; macOS can suppress prompt redisplay for an existing TCC decision. No OS prompt was visibly observed. The Issue's Scope and Acceptance Criteria do not require prompt redisplay, so this is recorded as a Tier-H limitation and remaining risk, not as a failed criterion and not as a claim that the prompt path is verified.
runs.demonstrates: The real AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions request path was executed through the production default with no seam substituted, and returned the documented immediate notTrusted state, matching the installed SDK's 'Prompting occurs asynchronously and does not affect the return value.' This satisfies the Issue Scope item 'request'.

runs.uiState: Taken while the System Settings Accessibility toggle named lowercase 'claude' was switched on. The reviewer switched it from off to on after explicit owner authorization and Touch ID, and the UI visibly showed it on.
runs.interpretation: The trusted transition was not observed for the probe process. The lowercase 'claude' UI row was not the effective TCC responsible identity of that Swift test process, so the toggle did not apply to it. This is a Tier-H verification limitation, not a product-code failure and not a passed trusted-transition test.
runs.scope: Author-created supplemental manual step. The canonical Issue does not require a same-process grant-to-revoke transition, so this run is non-blocking for acceptance.

runs.uiState: Taken after the reviewer restored the lowercase 'claude' toggle to off.
runs.interpretation: Identical to the toggle-on run, which is consistent with the toggle never having applied to this process. Because neither direction changed the observed outcome, the run is recorded as not demonstrating revoke either.
runs.scope: Author-created supplemental manual step. The canonical Issue does not require a same-process grant-to-revoke transition, so this run is non-blocking for acceptance.

grantRevokeConclusion.statement: Grant and revoke success for the actual Swift test process was not demonstrated. Toggling the lowercase 'claude' row on and then off produced outcome=notTrusted both times, so the UI row was not the probe process's effective TCC responsible identity.
grantRevokeConclusion.classification: Remaining Tier-H limitation and risk. It is not a product-code failure, no trusted-transition test is claimed as passed, and it does not block acceptance: the same-process grant-to-revoke transition is an author-created supplemental step that exceeds the canonical Issue's stated Scope and Acceptance Criteria.
grantRevokeConclusion.consistentWith: The identity-specific TCC behavior already documented in identityScope and in manual.md, and with the check run under the root / ChatGPT responsible identity returning trusted.
